text: Judas, Jesu Christi servus, Jacobi frater, sanctificatis in Deo Patre, et Jesu Christo reservatis, vocatis,
note: *Patrem/Patre/Pater/Patris* capital, God the Father (decision 20), as Jas 1:17, 1:27 and your *Deus et Pater*; 1573 lowers *pater* everywhere (ἐν θεῷ πατρί) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Illud autem vobis, quod semel didicistis, commemorare volo, quod Dominus, quum populum ex Aegypto servasset, rursum eos, qui non confiderant, perdidit:
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 1:3–4 state the occasion, and *Illud autem vōbīs … commemorāre volō* opens the three examples (Israel, the angels, Sodom; 1:5–7) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Similiter hi quoque somniantes, corpora habent polluta, et dominatum repudiant, dignitatibusque maledicunt.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): *Similiter hī quoque* applies the examples to the intruders (1:8–11); the BSB's break at 1:12 left, *Hī sunt* continuing the description (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Atqui Michael ille princeps angelus, quum disceptans cum diabolo, de Mosis corpore disputaret, non ausus est sententiam ferre maledicam, sed dixit: “Increpet te Dominus.”
note: Michael's words after *sed dīxit:* are direct (the jussive *increpet*): in “…”, as the BSB, *Increpet* capital as 1573 (*ſed dixit : Increpet te Dominus*, canvas 929); not in \\qt: the words are Zech 3:2's (*Increpet Dominus in te*), but here spoken by Michael in a story the Church Fathers took from the Assumption of Moses, not Scripture quoted by Jude; **uncertain** (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Vae eis, quoniam Cainiana via grassantur, et erroris Balaamici mercede profligati sunt, Coranaque coniuratione pereunt.
note: *Caīniānā*, *Balaamicī*, *Corānāque* capital, adjectives of names, as 1573 (*Cainiana via … Balaamici … Coranaque*, canvas 929) and your Heb 10:28 *Mōsaicam*, Acts 15:1 *Mōsaicō* (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: De his etiam vaticinatus est septimus ab Adamo Enochus, dicens:
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): *Dē hīs etiam vāticinātus est … Henōchus* introduces the prophecy (1:14–16), as the BSB; the BSB's break at 1:16 left, *Hī sunt* closing the prophecy's application (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: “Venturus est Dominus cum suis sanctis legionibus, ut in omnes judicium exerceat, omnesque eorum impios convincat omnium, quae patraverint, impie factorum, omniumque, quae contra eum atrociter dixerint, sontes, impii.”
note: Enoch's prophecy (1 Enoch 1:9) after 1:14's *dīcēns:* in “…”, as the BSB; the whole verse, *sontēs, impiī* the prophecy's last words (ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἀσεβεῖς); **not in \\qt and not set as poetry**, though the BSB sets it as verse: \\qt marks Scripture quoted (brief.md, Layout), and 1 Enoch is not in Castellio's Bible or the edition's canon; **uncertain**, yours to decide (\\qt and the BSB's four lines if you count it as Scripture cited) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Hi sunt, qui se ipsos secernunt, animales, Spiritum non habentes.
note: *Spīritum* capital, the Spirit of God (πνεῦμα μὴ ἔχοντες, BSB and NRSV "devoid of the Spirit"; decision 20), set against *animālēs* as in your 1 Cor 2:14; **uncertain**: 1573 *ſpiritum* and the KJV "having not the Spirit" (capital), Castellio's margin glosses *animales* (*c terreſtres*) only (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Vos vero, carissimi, in sanctissima vestra fide vos ipsos exaedificantes, sacro adflatu Deo supplicantes,
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): *Vōs vērō, cārissimī* turns from the scoffers to the readers (1:20–23); *sacrō afflātū* lower, as your *dīvīnō afflātū* (1 Cor 12:3, Eph 2:22, Acts 20:22); the BSB's break at 1:22 left, 1:20–23 one sentence (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: soli sapienti Deo Servatori nostro gloria et magnitudo, imperium et potentia, nunc et in omnia saecula: Amen.
note: *sōlī* lower case: the sentence of 1:24 (*Eī vērō, quī … potest,*) runs on after its comma; *Servātōrī nostrō* capital, God our Saviour (σωτῆρι ἡμῶν; decision 20 and 45), as Titus 1:3 (Claude, 2026-11-12)
